title: Cost-of-living protests and demonstrations held across France

tea.why: Protesters are demonstrating against rising expenses and school conditions amid broader cost-of-living pressures in France and Europe.
tea.want: Demonstrators demand relief from high living expenses and improvements to school conditions.
tea.changed: Oct 18: France’s interior minister reported at least 2,000 arrests and hundreds of injuries following weekend demonstrations.

summary: Hundreds of thousands of individuals participated in street demonstrations across France over the weekend, focusing on rising expenses and school conditions. While some protests involved violence and disruptions, such as in Paris, international governments issued travel warnings as unrest spread to neighboring European nations like Portugal, Italy, and Belgium. French authorities reported significant clashes, resulting in numerous arrests and injuries among law enforcement officers and firefighters. French President Emmanuel Macron stated that authorities might ban future demonstrations if deemed necessary, while organizers announced plans for additional protests scheduled for later in the month and in November.
response: According to the interior minister, at least 2,000 people have been arrested and over 600 law enforcement officers and firefighters injured. President Emmanuel Macron stated that authorities could ban future demonstrations if necessary.

arrests.text: At least 2,000 people have been arrested

injuries.text: more than 600 law enforcement officers and firefighters have been injured

updates.text: Protesters gathered in Paris and other locations for demonstrations.
Videos circulated showing street disturbances and fires near the Arc de Triomphe in Paris.
France’s interior minister stated that at least 2,000 people were arrested and over 600 officers and firefighters were injured over the weekend.
President Emmanuel Macron stated that authorities could ban upcoming demonstrations if necessary.
